title: Lesson 42 multiple-nucleus adjectival modification technical proof

groups.title: Multiple-nucleus rank reversal
groups.proposal: Use exact NNC and VNC Results in the canonical adjectival-modification owner, with the NNC core as principal head and the modifier clause as adjunct.
groups.readingJob: Show clause rank, shared referent contact, and the absence of an adjective-word source class.
groups.decisionSplit: Only topology, order, adjunctor, reference contact, or compound-head target may become choices.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer Nahuatl rank from English modifier and head word order.

groups.title: Preposed order and unit scope
groups.proposal: Keep ordinary and preposed modification in one owner; derive complete-sentence versus adjoined-unit scope from order and in-marking.
groups.readingJob: Show order, adjunctor attachment, hiatus behavior, and resulting unit scope.
groups.decisionSplit: Order and in-marking are selectable only when both structures are licensed.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not treat preposed modification as topicalization or detach in from its clause.

groups.title: Supplementation and modification ambiguity
groups.proposal: Keep supplementation and modification as separate canonical compositions even where the same clauses support both readings.
groups.readingJob: Show which nuclear element is the head and which clause is principal.
groups.decisionSplit: Expose a relation choice only when both complete typed analyses remain licensed.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not resolve the ambiguity from translation alone.

groups.title: Simple and compound heads
groups.proposal: Allow exact simple or compound NNC Results as heads and preserve the genuine matrix-versus-whole-compound modification target choice.
groups.readingJob: Show compound structure and whether the modifier targets its matrix or the whole compound.
groups.decisionSplit: Compound target is selectable only when both readings are licensed.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not assign target scope from physical adjacency or English gloss.

groups.title: VNC modifiers and reference contact
groups.proposal: Admit exact intransitive and transitive VNC Results as modifiers and validate subject-versus-object contact against typed participants.
groups.readingJob: Show modifier valence, participant contact, agreement, and remaining ambiguity.
groups.decisionSplit: Subject or object contact is selectable only for a transitive modifier with both licensed contacts.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not infer contact from animacy, translation, or proximity alone.

groups.title: NNC modifier and head lattice
groups.proposal: Admit exact adverbialized, cardinal, quantitive, ordinary, supplementation, pronominal, demonstrative, and measure Results through the same modification relation.
groups.readingJob: Show each original Source type, its current rank, and its shared-referent relation.
groups.decisionSplit: Head-versus-modifier rank is selectable only where both complete structures are licensed.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not create adjective variants of existing NNC classes.

groups.title: Recursive modification
groups.proposal: Allow an exact adjectival-modification Result to serve as the head of a larger modification without flattening or rebuilding it.
groups.readingJob: Show nested head identity, depth, and ordered clause structure.
groups.decisionSplit: No recursion-depth control is exposed; depth is derived from exact Result nesting.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not reconstruct recursion from a surface string.

groups.title: Incorporated modification structures
groups.proposal: Project an exact, typed, lexicalized modifier-plus-head Result into a compound embed while preserving constituent subjects, the modifier number dyad, and deletion of the head number dyad.
groups.readingJob: Show the exact source Result, internal boundary, retained subjects and modifier number, deleted head number, and outer compound owner.
groups.decisionSplit: Lexicalized-concatenate status must be supplied as typed Source analysis; Canvas example membership never licenses it.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not flatten a copied sentence string into a compound stem or whitelist the examples.
